-97.74270,30.30150.name: Fora Fertility, PLLC
-97.74270,30.30150.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Amanda Skillern, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-1.86094,38.99692.name: Instituto Bernabeu Albacete
-1.86094,38.99692.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-121.82330,38.44546.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-1.91142,52.45644.name: Priory Hospital
-1.91142,52.45644.state: The Priory Hospital, Priory Road, Edgbaston, Birmingham, B5 7UG, United Kingdom
-1.91142,52.45644.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-63.58013,44.63111.name: Saint Mary's University
-63.58013,44.63111.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, May 2024
-63.58013,44.63111.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, May 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-46.52543,-21.36970.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: https://crhwahibhassan.com.br/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

-71.08700,42.36600.name: Flagship Pioneering
-71.08700,42.36600.desc: Creates companies rather than investing in them, founding businesses around a technology and then staffing and funding them — Moderna among them. A venture firm that originates its own portfolio decides which biological ideas get a company built around them, which is a different kind of influence from choosing between proposals.

4.35250,50.84670.name: European Commission — ALURES animal use database
4.35250,50.84670.desc: The EU’s database of animal use across member states, by species, purpose and severity. It exists because a directive required it, and it is the only place a multi-country picture of laboratory animal use can be assembled at all.

4.35250,50.84670.name: EU Transparency Register — biotechnology lobbying
4.35250,50.84670.desc: Declared lobbying spend, staff and meetings for organisations seeking to influence EU institutions. Bayer reports roughly €6.5 million in its own name against about €26 million in association fees, so most of the money moves under an association’s name rather than a company’s.

-122.14900,37.39100.name: Exponent — regulatory and risk consulting
-122.14900,37.39100.desc: Provides the scientific analysis used in regulatory submissions and in litigation about them, for clients including agrochemical and biotechnology firms. Consulting science of this kind rarely appears in the public record even though it shapes what the record says.

-78.68210,35.78470.name: Camcore
-78.68210,35.78470.desc: A non-profit international tree breeding cooperative formed in 1980 by private industry and hosted at a public university, with 27 members across 11 countries in the Americas, Africa and Asia, working on pines, eucalypts, gmelina and teak. What distinguishes it from other tree improvement programmes is stated on its own front page: alongside breeding, a major emphasis on establishing EX SITU CONSERVATION PLANTINGS of species and populations, including several threatened species native to the southern United States. A breeding cooperative that also plants living archives of the populations it draws from is doing something the biobanks elsewhere in this facet do in freezers — and the trees keep evolving.

4.32600,52.03600.name: Kiwa
4.32600,52.03600.desc: Founded 1948, private, owned by the Dutch industrial holding company SHV, with 2023 revenue around €1.3bn and about 11,000 staff in more than 35 countries. Its organic arm certifies to the EU organic regulation, the US National Organic Program, the private Bio Suisse standard, the Naturland association's standard and a supermarket's own protocol, among others. That is the mechanism worth recording: a single commercial certifier holds the keys to a public regulation, a foreign government's programme, a farming association's private standard and a retailer's contractual requirement at the same time, and a producer meets all four through one auditor. Its growth since 2000 has been by acquisition — Gastec, Inspecta and Vinçotte among them.
